newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India marked lower, autos suffer.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India marked lower, autos suffer.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) were marked sharply lower in London on the back of poor first half earnings, slowing economic growth and a slide in the Bombay 30 share index below 3,000 points.
"The market makers talked the stock down but very few sellers really came out," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index lost 1.86 points, 3.06 percent, to 58.87 points, with the premium over the local market at 15.10 percent compared with yesterday's/Friday's 15.75 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 77.64 points or 2.55 percent to 2965.66.
The auto and truck sector was badly hit, Larsen & Toubro first half net profit rose 19 percent to two billion rupees and the GDR fell 69 cents to $13.00/$14.00.
Bajaj Auto fell $1.13 to $29.50/$31.00, Ashok Leyland dropped $1.38 to $8.00/$9.00, TELCO slid 63 cents to $10.25/$11.25 and Mahindra lost 32 cents to $10.00/$11.00.
Indian Petrochemicals first half net profit fell to 2.54 billion rupees from 3.05 and the GDR lost 56 cents to $7.75/$8.75.
"If you look at the dollar values and the premiums, there are some great bargains out there," said a trader.
Traders said that the launch of BPL Cellular's GDR had been delayed, and that the initial pricing range of $15.00-$17.00 had been cut to $10.00/$11.00.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 1.79 points, 2.64 percent, at 66.23, a premium of 29.35 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index fell 1.81 percent, or 13.45 points, to a provisional close of 731.46.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 1.61 points, 1.77 percent, at 92.66 a premium of 4.26 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index jumped 68.90 points or 1.03 percent higher at 6,761.39.
